subject: general
question: For how many years are the judges of the International Court of Justice elected?
solution:
The correct answer is __**9**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The judges of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) are elected for a term of **9 years**.
 
• They can be re-elected if they continue to meet the qualifications required.
 
• The ICJ consists of 15 judges, and elections are staggered so that one-third of the judges are elected every three years.
 
• The judges are elected by the United Nations General Assembly and the Security Council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Court of Justice (ICJ)**

 
 
• The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations (UN).
 
• It was established in June 1945 by the Charter of the United Nations and began work in April 1946.
 
• The court's role is to settle legal disputes submitted to it by states and to give advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by authorized UN organs and specialized agencies.
 
• The ICJ is located in The Hague, Netherlands.
 
 
 
• **Election Process**
 
 
• Judges are elected by the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council, where candidates must receive an absolute majority in both bodies.
 
• Elections are held every three years for one-third of the 15-member court, ensuring continuity within the ICJ.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for Judges**
 
 
• Judges must have a high moral character and possess the qualifications required in their respective countries for appointment to the highest judicial offices.
 
• Alternatively, they can be jurisconsults of recognized competence in international law.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction**
 
 
• The ICJ has jurisdiction to hear cases involving disputes between states, and it provides advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by UN organs and specialized agencies.
 
• Only states may be parties in cases before the ICJ.
